entities.summary:
Adeimantus of Collytus, son of Ariston of Athens, was an ancient Athenian Greek best known as Plato's brother. He plays an important part in Plato's Republic and is mentioned in the Apology and Parmenides dialogues. Born around 416 BCE, Adeimantus' life is marked by his involvement in Athenian politics and his association with the influential Athenian family. His connection to the Alcmaeonid dynasty, which ruled Athens from 506 to 506 BCE, lends depth to his significance. This familial tie, combined with his role in Plato's philosophical works, solidifies Adeimantus' place in the annals of ancient Greek history. Adeimantus' legacy extends beyond his brother's philosophical contributions, as he also participated in the Athenian democracy and was a member of the Athenian Assembly.

Adeimantus' involvement in Athenian politics was significant during the 5th century BCE, a time of great change and upheaval in the city-state. His association with the Alcmaeonid dynasty, which ruled Athens from 506 to 506 BCE, highlights the complex web of family ties and alliances that shaped Athenian politics. Adeimantus' participation in the Athenian democracy, as a member of the Athenian Assembly, underscores his commitment to the democratic ideals that defined ancient Athens.

Adeimantus' connection to Plato's philosophical works is well-documented, and his role in the Republic and Apology dialogues has been the subject of much scholarly debate. The significance of Adeimantus' contribution to Plato's philosophy lies in his ability to provide a unique perspective on the Athenian political system, one that is informed by his own experiences as a member of the Alcmaeonid dynasty. This perspective, in turn, has shed light on the complexities of Athenian politics during this period.
